**Rationale:** The claim commits a core correlation-vs-causation error by asserting that temporal precedence of measurement "proves" causation. While the All Our Families study uses a cross-lagged panel design (which is stronger than simple cross-sectional analysis), observational data with maternal self-report cannot establish causation. Unmeasured confounders (parental factors, socioeconomic status, home environment) remain plausible alternative explanations. The temporal ordering of measurements is necessary but insufficient for causal proof in an observational cohort without experimental manipulation or robust causal identification strategies.
